title: Skill scorecard
description: Outcome metrics from the warehouse. Operational signals are on 'Skill telemetry'. Below 30 merged PRs per arm no comparison is supportable — see docs/evaluation-power.md.

panels.title: Skill scorecard — pass rate with vs without, and the recommended action
panels.description: The primary metric. recommended_action is 'insufficient-data' whenever an arm is below 30 merged PRs or has no outcome data at all — that is a refusal, not a verdict.

targets.rawSql:
-- Weekly skill scorecard (design §4.5). Parameters: $__timeFrom(), $__timeTo()
WITH inv AS (
  SELECT * FROM skill_invocation WHERE started_at >= $__timeFrom() AND started_at < $__timeTo()
),
-- first-time policy pass for each PR/policy the skill is coupled with
first_run AS (
  SELECT pr_id, policy_id, passed FROM policy_result WHERE run_seq = 1
),
pr_skill AS (   -- PRs whose ticket had ≥1 invocation of the skill
  SELECT DISTINCT p.pr_id, i.skill_name, i.skill_version, i.harness
  FROM pull_request p JOIN inv i ON i.ticket_id = p.ticket_id
),
-- the policies each skill is accountable for, one row per (skill, version, policy)
skill_policy AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT skill_name, skill_version, unnest(policy_ids) AS policy_id FROM inv
),
-- A PR passes first time when EVERY policy the skill is accountable for passed on
-- run_seq = 1. Aggregating to one row per PR first is the whole point: the metric
-- is "first-time pass rate on the PR", so the PR is the unit. Averaging over the
-- join directly counted each PR once per invocation and reported n_with = 3192
-- against 120 merged PRs (#23).
pr_pass_with AS (
  SELECT ps.skill_name, ps.skill_version, ps.harness, ps.pr_id,
         MIN(CASE WHEN fr.passed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pr_passed
  FROM pr_skill ps
  JOIN skill_policy sp
    ON sp.skill_name = ps.skill_name AND sp.skill_version = ps.skill_version
  JOIN first_run fr
    ON fr.pr_id = ps.pr_id AND fr.policy_id = sp.policy_id
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
),
pass_with AS (
  SELECT skill_name, skill_version, harness,
         AVG(pr_passed::numeric) AS first_pass_rate_with,
         COUNT(*) AS n_with                      -- PRs, never invocations
  FROM pr_pass_with GROUP BY 1,2,3
),
-- the same measure over PRs in the window that did NOT use the skill
pr_pass_without AS (
  SELECT sp.skill_name, p.pr_id,
         MIN(CASE WHEN fr.passed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pr_passed
  FROM skill_policy sp
  JOIN first_run fr ON fr.policy_id = sp.policy_id
  JOIN pull_request p ON p.pr_id = fr.pr_id
  WHERE p.opened_at >= $__timeFrom() AND p.opened_at < $__timeTo()
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pr_skill ps WHERE ps.pr_id = p.pr_id AND ps.skill_name = sp.skill_name)
  GROUP BY 1,2
),
pass_without AS (
  SELECT skill_name, AVG(pr_passed::numeric) AS first_pass_rate_without,
         COUNT(*) AS n_without                   -- PRs, never invocations
  FROM pr_pass_without GROUP BY 1
),
overlap AS (   -- redundancy: co-invocation with other skills in the same session
  SELECT a.skill_name, COUNT(DISTINCT b.skill_name) AS co_invoked_skills
  FROM inv a JOIN inv b ON a.session_id = b.session_id AND a.skill_name <> b.skill_name
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
  i.skill_name, i.skill_version, i.harness,
  COUNT(*)                                            AS invocations,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.user_hash)                         AS distinct_users,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.session_id)                        AS sessions,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY i.load_tokens) AS p50_load_tokens,
  PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY i.tail_tokens) AS p50_tail_tokens,
  SUM(i.load_tokens + i.tail_tokens)                  AS total_tokens,
  AVG(CASE WHEN i.is_error THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)         AS error_rate,
  AVG(CASE WHEN i.llm_requests = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abandonment_rate,
  pw.first_pass_rate_with, pw.n_with,
  pwo.first_pass_rate_without, pwo.n_without,
  COALESCE(o.co_invoked_skills, 0)                    AS co_invoked_skills,
  CASE
    -- Insufficient data is checked FIRST and is not a verdict about the skill.
    -- 30 merged PRs per arm is the floor from docs/evaluation-power.md; below
    -- it no comparative claim is supportable, and 'keep' used to be returned
    -- for a skill with no outcome data at all (#23).
    WHEN pw.first_pass_rate_with IS NULL OR pwo.first_pass_rate_without IS NULL
      THEN 'insufficient-data'
    WHEN COALESCE(pw.n_with, 0) < 30 OR COALESCE(pwo.n_without, 0) < 30
      THEN 'insufficient-data'
    WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 'deprecate'
    WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT i.user_hash) = 1 THEN 'review-single-user'
    WHEN pw.first_pass_rate_with < pwo.first_pass_rate_without THEN 'refine'
    WHEN COALESCE(o.co_invoked_skills, 0) >= 3 THEN 'review-merge'
    ELSE 'keep'
  END AS recommended_action
FROM inv i
LEFT JOIN pass_with pw ON pw.skill_name = i.skill_name AND pw.skill_version = i.skill_version AND pw.harness = i.harness
LEFT JOIN pass_without pwo ON pwo.skill_name = i.skill_name
LEFT JOIN overlap o ON o.skill_name = i.skill_name
GROUP BY 1,2,3, pw.first_pass_rate_with, pw.n_with, pwo.first_pass_rate_without, pwo.n_without, o.co_invoked_skills
ORDER BY total_tokens DESC

panels.title: First-time pass rate by arm
panels.description: Read the PR count beside the rate. A rate over few PRs is descriptive only.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT t.harness_arm AS arm,
       avg(CASE WHEN pr.passed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS first_time_pass_rate,
       count(DISTINCT pr.pr_id) AS prs
FROM policy_result pr
JOIN pull_request p ON p.pr_id = pr.pr_id
JOIN ticket t ON t.ticket_id = p.ticket_id
WHERE pr.run_seq = 1 AND p.merged_at IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Tokens per merged PR (total spend, not skill-attributed)
panels.description: Uses session_cost, which is total spend. skill_invocation.tail_tokens is only the share one skill could claim; the two must never be summed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT t.harness_arm AS arm,
       sum(sc.input_tokens + sc.output_tokens)::numeric
         / NULLIF(count(DISTINCT p.pr_id), 0) AS tokens_per_pr,
       count(DISTINCT p.pr_id) AS prs
FROM session_cost sc
JOIN pull_request p ON p.ticket_id = sc.ticket_id AND p.merged_at IS NOT NULL
JOIN ticket t ON t.ticket_id = p.ticket_id
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Data quality — these bound every conclusion
panels.description: Both are fixable only while the work is happening: a branch renamed tomorrow does not retroactively attribute today's PRs. Unattributed rows are kept for cost and excluded from outcome analysis.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 'unattributed sessions (no ticket key on the branch)' AS issue,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE ticket_id = 'unattributed') AS affected,
       count(*) AS total
FROM session_cost
UNION ALL
SELECT 'unversioned skills (not in the catalogue)',
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE skill_version = 'unversioned'), count(*)
FROM skill_invocation
UNION ALL
-- The version is asserted by the front-matter; content_hash is observed. More
-- than one hash under one version means the guidance changed without a bump, so
-- that row of the scorecard is aggregating two different populations.
SELECT 'skills edited without a version bump',
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE v.hashes > 1), count(*)
FROM (SELECT skill_name, skill_version, count(DISTINCT content_hash) AS hashes
      FROM skill_invocation WHERE content_hash IS NOT NULL
      GROUP BY 1, 2) v

panels.title: Tokens by artefact kind (never sum these rows)
panels.description: ADR-009. Sub-agent cache reads are large by construction — the agent re-reads its parent's context on every request — so they are shown apart from everything else. `without_usage` is how many rows carried no token figures at all; a total over three observed rows is a different claim from one over three hundred.

targets.rawSql:
-- Where the spend goes, by artefact. Kinds overlap deliberately: a skill's
-- tail is inside the turn that loaded it, and a sub-agent's tokens are inside
-- the turn that spawned it. Compare the rows; never add them up.
SELECT kind,
       count(*)                                   AS activations,
       count(DISTINCT prompt_id) FILTER (WHERE kind = 'turn') AS turns,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE input_tokens IS NULL)           AS without_usage,
       sum(coalesce(input_tokens, 0) + coalesce(output_tokens, 0)
           + coalesce(cache_creation_tokens, 0))  AS tokens_excl_cache_read,
       sum(coalesce(cache_read_tokens, 0))        AS cache_read_tokens
FROM artefact_activation
WHERE started_at BETWEEN $__timeFrom() AND $__timeTo()
GROUP BY kind
ORDER BY tokens_excl_cache_read DESC NULLS LAST;

panels.title: Loader freshness — how old is everything above?
panels.description: Every panel on this dashboard is as old as the last successful loader run. A run that failed still writes a row, because a loader that records only its successes cannot be told from one nobody ever ran.

targets.rawSql:
-- How stale is this dashboard? Spans reach Tempo when a hook fires; they reach
-- this warehouse only when a loader runs. Tempo once held four days of spans
-- Postgres had never seen, and every component reported success throughout.
SELECT loader,
       max(finished_at)                                        AS last_run,
       round(extract(epoch FROM (now() - max(finished_at))) / 60) AS minutes_ago,
       max(source_max_ts)                                      AS newest_row_loaded,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM loader_run r2
         WHERE r2.loader = loader_run.loader AND NOT r2.ok
           AND r2.started_at > now() - interval '24 hours')    AS failures_24h
FROM loader_run
GROUP BY loader
ORDER BY loader;
